issue_paraphrase: If uv's on-disk HTTP cache entry is corrupted so that the trailing length marker encodes an enormous value, the program crashes with a Rust arithmetic-overflow panic (a backtrace ending in 'attempt to add with overflow') instead of treating the entry as corrupt and re-fetching, on any operation that reads the cached HTTP responses such as refreshing package index metadata or resolving dependencies. A user whose cache file got truncated or mangled (crashed disk, interrupted write) can be stuck with startup crashes instead of a graceful recovery.
fix_summary: In deserialize_cache_policy_len, replace the `bytes.len() < len_usize + 8` guard (which itself overflows when len_usize == usize::MAX) with a check that the declared policy length fits in the available buffer before any arithmetic, returning the existing ArchiveRead error for malformed entries. Adds a unit test that feeds 8 bytes of 0xFF and asserts an ArchiveRead error kind instead of a panic.

issue_paraphrase: The space-savings figure printed by uv's cache cleanup commands is wrong in common situations: when a cached file is a hard link to a file that still exists somewhere else, uv reports the full file size as reclaimed even though no space was actually freed, and it reports the logical length of files instead of the disk blocks they occupy, so sparse files and small files also over- or under-report the real savings. Users running `uv cache clean` or `uv cache prune` see a byte figure such as '(1.0MiB)' that does not match what was actually reclaimed, which makes capacity planning and CI space accounting misleading.
fix_summary: Replaces the logical-length accounting (`metadata.len()`) with a block-based estimate (st_blocks * 512 when the link count is 1, 0 otherwise), so storage is counted once for hard-linked files (only when its last link is removed) and holes/non-allocated blocks of sparse files are not charged; renames the summary fields logical_bytes/physical_bytes to coarse_bytes/fine_bytes and the mode enum RemovalMode to RemovalAccounting. Adds crate-level regression tests (crates/uv-cache/tests/removal.rs, 4 tests) plus CLI snapshot updates in crates/uv/tests/build/cache_clean.rs and cache_prune.rs.

issue_paraphrase: A Python version file (`.python-version` or `.python-versions`) whose entries carry leading or trailing whitespace - for example lines like " python3.12 " or entries separated by tabs - causes uv to silently ignore those entries. Instead of being read as version requests, the padded lines are treated as unsupported executable names, a warning is printed for each, and the requested Python version is never selected, so commands that depend on the pin pick a different interpreter or fail. A version file that is perfectly valid except for incidental indentation behaves as if it were empty, and the only hint is a warning that the request is 'unsupported'.
fix_summary: Trim each line of the version file before filtering comments and parsing: `content.lines().map(str::trim).filter(...).map(PythonRequest::parse)` (replacing a per-line `line.trim()` inside the comment check on the raw line), so padded entries parse as version requests, and drops an intermediate allocation. Extends the `python_pin_with_comments` integration test (renamed python_pin_with_comments_and_whitespace) to cover spaces, tabs, whitespace-only lines and indented comments for both version-file names.
